newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica seeks annual sugar quota with Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica seeks annual sugar quota with Venezuela.

text.p: Costa Rica is negotiating an annual sugar quota with Venezuela to the tune of 15,000 tonnes, Trade Minister Jose Manuel Salazar said.
"We have started to negotiate a reduction in tariffs and an annual sugar quota and now we are waiting for a reply from the Venezuelan authorities," Salazar told a media conference.
Salazar explained that Venezuela currently makes up its sugar demands by importing from various nations.
He gave no net tonnage of imports but said Central American nations supply Caracas with 30 percent of its import needs and the remaining 70 percent is supplied by nations from outside the region.
"We are looking to claim part of this 30 percent, a minimum of 15,000 tonnes," he added. Currently, Costa Rica does not export sugar to Venezuela.

Costa Rica's sugar cane growers association, the Liga Agricola Industrial de la Cana de Azucar, recently said that the 1996-1997 harvest will produce 3.5 million tonnes of cane, yielding 350,000 tonnes of sugar.
